role: Manager, Western Exploration, AMAX Exploration, Inc.
stance_basis: letter requesting country-wide general permit exemption for mineral exploration from per-event ORV permit requirement
summary: H. T. Schassberger, Manager of Western Exploration at AMAX Exploration, Inc., submitted a letter arguing that the four-month advance permit requirement for ORV events would cause costly delays to legitimate mineral exploration on public lands. He proposed that a country-wide general permit be issued to those engaged in legitimate mineral exploration, covering both corporate exploration groups and individual prospectors who derive significant livelihood from prospecting, so as to eliminate the need for a permit for each ORV event.
complaint_summary: Schassberger argues that the four-month advance permit requirement for ORV events will cause expensive delays to legitimate mineral exploration on public lands, and requests a country-wide general permit for mineral explorers to eliminate the need for individual event permits.

statement.text:
We have read Executive Order 11644 and the Draft Environmental Statement, (Int Des 72-62) dated May 26, 1972, and make the following comments for your consideration.
As you are aware, much mineral exploration activity in the western U. S. is focused on public lands and, in many cases, such activity is carried out through use of four-wheel drive vehicles on old logging and/or mining roads which give access to hinterland areas. Additionally, in the normal course of events in minerals exploration, it is usually not possible to determine far in advance what specific areas are to be considered.
The requirement that permits for ORV events "...shall be submitted no less than four months, or a lesser time as each Bureau may determine, in advance..." will cause innumerable, expensive delays to those engaged in legitimate minerals exploration on public lands if the logging and mining roads are considered to be "off established roadways" (U.S. Dept. of Interior Memorandum K14 dated May 5, 1972).
We suggest, therefore, that provision be made for issuance of a country-wide general permit to those engaged in legitimate mineral exploration to eliminate the need for a permit for each ORV event; legitimate mineral exploration (activity) being defined to include both members of corporate
